Figure 4:Overview of VIVID.All branches share prefixes from the non-contrast student’s rollouts. An auxiliary branch mixes paired enhanced-image values into attention-weight-selected visual positions. The induced prediction shift guides a positive projection of the teacher’s correction in centered log-probability space to construct the distillation target.

Figure 12:Qualitative comparisons of SFT, OPSD, and VIVID across three datasets.Examples show model-generated evidence and answers for liver CT, brain MRI, and breast MRI. Checkmarks and crosses indicate correct and incorrect answers, respectively. Margin selectivity is reported alongside each response, and top-1–top-2 probability margins are shown for highlighted evidence tokens, both in percentage points. VIVID corrects baseline errors and exhibits higher margin selectivity in these examples. Even when methods produce the same correct answer, VIVID assigns a larger probability margin to the highlighted answer-relevant token.
